definition: Retrospective means looking back on or dealing with past events and situations.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word retrospective. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know retrospective should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The clinic's retrospective review of five years of patient charts revealed which treatments had actually helped.
Reminiscent is gentler than retrospective — usually something is reminiscent of the past, evoking a few memories in passing, while a retrospective review deliberately examines a whole stretch of it.
Elegiac is more intense than retrospective — an elegiac poem doesn't just look back at what happened, it openly mourns what is gone.

Backward-looking means focused on the past, and it often carries a sniff of criticism — a backward-looking policy resists whatever comes next. Retrospective is neutral and deliberate: a retrospective review examines the past on purpose to learn from it. Backward-looking is an orientation; retrospective is an activity.

Reflective means thoughtfully reviewing what has happened — a quiet, musing frame of mind a person falls into. Retrospective is more structured: it names a deliberate look back across a defined stretch of the past, like a report or exhibit. A person feels reflective; a review is retrospective.

Nostalgic means feeling a bittersweet, affectionate longing for a past time — it names an emotion. Retrospective is cool and workmanlike: a retrospective report examines the past without necessarily missing it at all. Nostalgic is how looking back can feel; retrospective names the act of reviewing.

Retrospective means looking back on or dealing with past events and situations.
In a retrospective essay for the paper's final issue, the graduating editor looked back on four years of late-night deadlines and hard-won lessons.
The essay examines events that already happened — four years of the editor's own past — which is precisely what makes it retrospective.
This course teaches retrospective as an adjective ('a retrospective report,' 'a retrospective glance').
You may also meet it as a noun — 'a retrospective' is an exhibit reviewing an artist's whole career.
Watch the near-twin retroactive: a retroactive rule reaches back to take effect from a past date, while something retrospective looks back to examine the past.
Reviewing versus rule-changing — keep them separate.

Twenty years after the wolves were released, the park service commissioned a retrospective assessment of the whole program.
The team was not asked how the packs were doing now; it was asked to look back across two decades and judge what each decision had produced.
Rangers pulled old collar data, weather logs, and the notebooks of biologists long since retired.
The final report praised some early choices and flagged others that had nearly sunk the effort in its third winter.
